memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "'The priest shall burn them on the altar as a food offering presented to the LORD. It is a guilt offering. Any male in a priest's family may eat it, but it must be eaten in the sanctuary area; it is most holy.'" - Lev 7:5-6 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
It is a guilt offering. God names it plainly. He does not soften the label to spare anyone's feelings.

There is something healthy in that. We live in a time that struggles enormously with the word guilt. We rename it — stress, regret, poor choices, a difficult season. Sometimes those words are accurate. Often they are avoidance.

Real guilt is not a disease to be cured or an emotion to be managed. It is information. It tells you something true happened, and it points toward a remedy.

The trouble is that guilt without a remedy is unbearable, so people learn to deny it rather than carry it. That is understandable. But the answer is not to pretend the guilt is unreal. The answer is to know there is an offering.

Paul distinguishes two kinds: Godly sorrow brings repentance that leads to salvation and leaves no regret, but worldly sorrow brings death (2 Cor 7:10). One kind moves you toward God and ends. The other circles endlessly and destroys.

If you feel guilt today, do not talk yourself out of it and do not drown in it. Take it where it was always meant to go.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do I rename my guilt rather than face it?
2. Am I carrying guilt in circles instead of bringing it to the cross?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, I will not pretend my guilt away or be crushed by it. I bring it to Christ, who is my offering. Amen.
